findings.title: The canonical Connect contract is not identified
findings.details: The issue permits either implementing or bridging to an unspecified canonical contract. It must identify the authoritative proto path, package and service version, methods, request/response semantics, compatibility baseline, and generated-code ownership. Owner decision required: which exact protocol contract must the implementation expose?

findings.title: Scoped-state and persistence semantics are incomplete
findings.details: The precedence expression does not define scope identifiers, inheritance and fallback, per-operation read/write behavior, reset or deletion, storage ownership, session lifetime, reload boundaries, atomicity, concurrency, or handling of unavailable and corrupt persisted state. Owner decision required: define these semantics and the authoritative persistence boundary.

findings.title: Trust, validation, and failure boundaries are unspecified
findings.details: The contract does not state who may read or mutate each scope, where axes and options are validated, how Connect and REST errors map, or what happens when registry and persistence operations disagree or partially fail. Owner decision required: define caller authority, validation ownership, error mappings, and fail-closed or recovery behavior.

findings.title: Dependency sequencing and single-lane ownership are unresolved
findings.details: The issue overlaps gateway naming, registry, OAuth dispatch, and packaging work represented by issues 210, 211, 213, and 214, but declares no dependency order, interface boundary, or exclusive ownership. Owner decision required: specify which issue owns shared contracts and the sequencing or blocking relationships among these lanes.

findings.title: REST compatibility is left as an implementation-time product decision
findings.details: The requirement says REST shims may be kept if needed, while acceptance says REST is demoted to a shim. It does not decide whether REST is retained, which routes and behavior remain compatible, how long compatibility lasts, how clients migrate, or which breaking changes are permitted. Owner decision required: approve the compatibility and deprecation policy.

findings.title: Acceptance, evidence, rollout, and rollback are not objective
findings.details: The acceptance statement does not enumerate operation-level cases, authoritative test commands, exact documentation targets, process-reload evidence, compatibility checks, rollout stages, or rollback criteria. The listed test topics alone cannot prove the stable control-plane contract or safe migration. Owner decision required: approve measurable acceptance cases and release evidence.
